prompt.value: Select the recursive function member(L, x) that returns True if x is present in list L, and False otherwise, including when L is empty.

explanation.value:
Let us look at the correct solution: def member(L, x): if len(L) == 0: return False if len(L) == 1: return
L[0] == x return (L[0] == x) or member(L[1 : ], x) The basic idea of the solution is to divide the list into two parts:
first element rest of the list after ignoring the first element If happens to be the first element of the list, we are
done. If is not present at index 0 in the list, then we have to check if it is present in the remainder of the list.
Recursive part To check whether is present in the remainder of the list, we use a recursive call member(L[1: ], x) is
the list after ignoring the first element. The two conditions are joined together by . Note that it is not condition.
We don't need to be present in both the first position and in the rest of the list. return (L[0] == x) or member(L[1
: ], x) # recursive call Base case There are essentially two conditions to check: Empty list Singleton list if len(L) ==
0: return False if len(L) == 1: return L[0] == x
